name: Unicode canonical equivalence
problem: Visually matching text can use different code-point sequences and fail a direct string comparison.

origin.summary: Historical priority, inventor and first adoption remain unresolved. The cited primary documentation establishes the described mechanism, not its invention.

mechanism: Normalization maps text to a chosen Unicode normalization form before comparison. Canonical normalization differs from compatibility folding and from locale-sensitive collation.
solutionFamily: Normalized text comparison versus raw code units
costs: Normalization costs work and can alter representation.
Compatibility or locale policy may be wrong for identifiers.
transferRule: Specify normalization, case and locale policies independently.
confidence: MEDIUM: mechanism anchored to primary documentation; historical attribution and unknown language cells unresolved; traces are editorial reasoning examples.
examples: JavaScript: '\u00e9' and 'e\u0301' have different raw sequences; normalize('NFC') makes their canonical forms compare equal.
counterexamples: Normalization does not make all look-alike characters equal or automatically implement case-insensitive matching.

assessment.prompt: Two user names look identical but compare unequal. Design a comparison policy without collapsing every visual confusable.
rubric: Keep security/confusable policy separate from normalization.
